questions.question_text: Which of the following errors is not disclosed by a Trial Balance?
options: C) Wrong balancing of an account
D) Posting on the wrong side of an account
questions.answer: B) Error of complete omission

questions.question_text: Under the straight-line method of depreciation, the amount of depreciation charged each year:
questions.answer: C) Remains constant

questions.question_text: A Suspense Account is generally opened to rectify:
questions.answer: D) One-sided errors

questions.question_text: Wages paid for the installation of a new machinery should be debited to:
questions.answer: B) Machinery Account

questions.question_text: Closing stock given inside the Trial Balance is shown in:
options: D) Both Trading Account and Balance Sheet
questions.answer: C) Balance Sheet only

questions.question_text: A reserve created out of normal business operations and kept secret is known as a:
questions.answer: C) Secret Reserve

questions.question_text: Prepaid rent appearing in the trial balance is treated as:
questions.answer: B) An Asset

questions.question_text: Under the Written Down Value method, depreciation is calculated on:
options: C) Book Value at the beginning of the year
questions.answer: C) Book Value at the beginning of the year

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an example of a Capital Expenditure?
options: B) Purchase of goods for resale
C) Extension of the factory building
questions.answer: C) Extension of the factory building

questions.question_text: Goods given as free samples are credited to:
questions.answer: C) Purchases Account

questions.question_text: An amount of $500 received from a debtor previously written off as a bad debt is credited to:
questions.answer: B) Bad Debts Recovered Account

questions.question_text: The primary purpose of preparing a Trial Balance is to check the:
options: A) Arithmetical accuracy of the books
B) Financial position of the business
questions.answer: A) Arithmetical accuracy of the books

questions.question_text: Provision for Bad and Doubtful Debts is created based on the principle of:
questions.answer: B) Conservatism (Prudence)

questions.question_text: If a manager is entitled to a 5% commission on net profit *after* charging such commission, the formula is:
questions.answer: B) Net Profit x (5 / 105)

questions.question_text: An error of principle involves:
options: A) Wrong casting of subsidiary books
B) Wrong posting to a personal account
C) Recording capital expenditure as revenue expenditure
D) Omission of a transaction completely
questions.answer: C) Recording capital expenditure as revenue expenditure

questions.question_text: Outstanding wages given in the adjustments will be shown in:
options: D) Both Trading Account and Balance Sheet
questions.answer: D) Both Trading Account and Balance Sheet

questions.question_text: Marshalling of Balance Sheet refers to:
options: B) Arranging assets and liabilities in a specific order
questions.answer: B) Arranging assets and liabilities in a specific order

questions.question_text: Interest on drawings is treated as:
questions.answer: C) Income for the business

questions.question_text: Sale of old furniture recorded in the Sales Book is an example of:
questions.answer: A) Error of principle

questions.question_text: Depreciation is a process of:
options: B) Allocation of cost over useful life
questions.answer: B) Allocation of cost over useful life

questions.question_text: Differentiate between a Provision and a Reserve based on their fundamental purpose. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: A provision is a charge against profit created for a known liability of uncertain amount, whereas a reserve is an appropriation of profit meant for unknown future contingencies.

questions.question_text: State the accounting treatment when goods are withdrawn by the proprietor for personal use. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Goods withdrawn for personal use are debited to the Drawings Account and credited to the Purchases Account, effectively reducing the net purchases in the Trading Account.

questions.question_text: Define an Error of Commission and provide one brief example. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: An error of commission occurs when incorrect amounts are recorded, posted, or totalled. For example, a sale of $500 posted to a debtor's account as $50.

questions.question_text: Explain how accrued income given in the adjustments is handled in the final accounts. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Accrued income is added to the respective income on the credit side of the Profit & Loss Account and is also shown on the asset side of the Balance Sheet.

questions.question_text: Why does a business entity charge depreciation on its fixed assets? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Depreciation is charged to allocate the asset's cost over its useful life, matching expenses against revenues to calculate accurate net profit and present a true financial position.

questions.question_text: What does a debit balance in a Suspense Account signify before final accounts preparation? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: A debit balance in a Suspense Account signifies that the credit side of the Trial Balance was heavier than the debit side before rectification of one-sided errors.

questions.question_text: Rectify the following error: Goods sold to Mohan for $4,500 were mistakenly passed through the Purchases Book. Provide the correct journal entry. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Debit Mohan's Account with $9,000. Credit the Purchases Account with $4,500 to cancel the wrong entry, and credit the Sales Account with $4,500 to record the correct sale, rectifying the entire transaction.

questions.question_text: A machine was purchased for $12,000, but $1,000 spent on its installation was debited to the Wages Account. Pass the rectifying entry. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: To rectify this error of principle, debit the Machinery Account with $1,000 to capitalize the installation cost, and credit the Wages Account with $1,000 to remove the incorrectly charged revenue expense.

questions.question_text: Calculate depreciation for the first year using the Straight Line Method: Asset cost $45,000, installation $5,000, estimated scrap value $5,000, and useful life 10 years. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: The total asset cost is $50,000 ($45,000 + $5,000). Deducting the scrap value ($5,000) leaves a depreciable base of $45,000. Dividing by the 10-year useful life yields an annual depreciation charge of $4,500.

questions.question_text: Explain the treatment of Manager's Commission calculated at 10% on net profit before charging such commission, assuming a pre-commission profit of $55,000. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Calculate the commission as 10% of $55,000, which equals $5,500. Debit this $5,500 to the Profit & Loss Account as an expense and show it as an outstanding liability on the Balance Sheet.

questions.question_text: The total of the Sales Return Book was undercast by $2,000. Pass the rectifying journal entry utilizing a Suspense Account. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Since the Sales Return Account has a debit balance and was undercast, debit the Sales Return Account with $2,000. Credit the Suspense Account with $2,000 to complete the double entry and balance the ledger.

questions.question_text: An old furniture piece with a book value of $6,000 was sold for $4,500. Provide the journal entry to record this disposal and the resulting loss. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Debit the Cash Account with $4,500 for the proceeds. Debit the Profit & Loss Account (or Loss on Sale of Asset) with $1,500. Credit the Furniture Account with $6,000 to remove the asset.

questions.question_text: Provide the adjusting entries for Outstanding Salary of $3,000 and Prepaid Insurance of $1,200 at the end of the financial year. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: For salary: Debit Salary Account $3,000, Credit Outstanding Salary $3,000. For insurance: Debit Prepaid Insurance $1,200, Credit Insurance Account $1,200. These ensure expenses match the current year revenues accurately.

questions.question_text: Briefly describe how to present 'Life Insurance Premium' paid by a sole proprietor out of business funds in the Final Accounts. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Life Insurance Premium paid for the owner is treated as personal Drawings, not a business expense. It must be deducted directly from the proprietor's Capital on the liabilities side of the Balance Sheet.

sections.section_name: Section D - Long Answer (LA) / Problem Solving

questions.question_text: From a Trial Balance, Debtors are $60,000. Adjustments require writing off further bad debts of $4,000 and creating a 5% Provision for Doubtful Debts. Describe the exact step-by-step P&L and Balance Sheet layout. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: First, deduct further bad debts of $4,000 from $60,000 debtors, leaving $56,000. Calculate the 5% provision on $56,000, which is $2,800. In the P&L debit side, add $4,000 further bad debts and $2,800 new provision. In the Balance Sheet, show Debtors at $56,000 minus the $2,800 provision, netting $53,200.

questions.question_text: A plant costing $100,000 was purchased on April 1, 2024. Depreciation is charged at 10% p.a. using the Written Down Value method. Describe the calculation steps to find the plant's book value on March 31, 2026. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: For the first year ending March 2025, calculate 10% on $100,000, yielding $10,000 depreciation and a $90,000 WDV balance. For the second year ending March 2026, calculate 10% on the new $90,000 base, yielding $9,000 depreciation. Subtracting $9,000 from $90,000 gives a final book value of $81,000.

questions.question_text: A bookkeeper found a $1,500 difference in the Trial Balance and placed it on the debit side of a Suspense Account. Later, they found a $2,000 credit purchase was entirely omitted, and a $500 cash sale was posted to the credit of Sales but omitted from Cash. Describe the rectification. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: The omitted credit purchase is a two-sided error: debit Purchases $2,000 and credit Creditors $2,000 (does not affect Suspense). The omitted cash debit is a one-sided error: debit Cash Account $500 and credit Suspense Account $500. This $500 credit partially clears the original $1,500 debit balance in the Suspense Account.

questions.question_text: Prepare the layout logic for a Sole Proprietorship Trading Account closing entries. The Trial Balance shows Opening Stock $20k, Purchases $80k, Sales $150k, and Wages $10k. Closing Stock is valued at $25k outside the Trial Balance. Determine Gross Profit. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Debit the Trading Account with Opening Stock ($20k), Purchases ($80k), and Wages ($10k), totaling $110k in direct charges. Credit the Trading Account with Sales ($150k) and Closing Stock ($25k), totaling $175k. The difference ($175k credit minus $110k debit) results in a Gross Profit of $65k transferred to the P&L.
